/-!
# Conjecture 5.16

by F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III

Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?
Baumslag, Cannonito, and Miller proved this when the degrees of the local linear
representations are bounded, with the stronger conclusion that the containing
finitely presented group has solvable word problem.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.16»

/-- A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group with finitely
many generators and finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/--
Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?

Here locally linear means that every finitely generated subgroup $H$ has a
faithful finite-dimensional representation $H \to \operatorname{GL}_n(F)$.
The field $F$ and the degree $n$ may depend on $H$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G],
      (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
        ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (n : ℕ)
          (ρ : H →* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F), Function.Injective ρ) →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresented P ∧
        ∃ ι : G →* P, Function.Injective ι := by
  sorry

/--
Baumslag, Cannonito, and Miller proved that every countable locally linear group
of bounded degree embeds in a finitely presented group with solvable word
problem. Bounded degree means that one degree $n$ works for every finitely
generated subgroup, while the field may depend on the subgroup.

The conclusion below records the finitely-presented embedding supplied by their
theorem. The stronger solvable-word-problem conclusion is omitted because the
required computability notion for group presentations is not available in
Mathlib.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16».variants.bounded_degree :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G],
      (∃ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
        ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F)
          (ρ : H →* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F), Function.Injective ρ) →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresented P ∧
        ∃ ι : G →* P, Function.Injective ι := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.16»

/-!
# Conjecture 5.16

by F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III

Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?
Baumslag, Cannonito, and Miller proved the bounded-degree case, with a target group
having solvable word problem.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.16»

/-- A group is linear if it embeds in the general linear group of some finite degree over some
field. -/
def IsLinear (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (n : ℕ) (φ : G →* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F),
    Function.Injective φ

/-- A group is locally linear if each of its finitely generated subgroups is linear. The field and
the degree may depend on the subgroup. -/
def IsLocallyLinear (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsLinear H

/-- A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a quotient of a free group on finitely many
generators by the normal closure of finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- A finitely presented group has solvable word problem if it admits a finite presentation for
which membership in the normal closure of the relators is a computable predicate on signed words.
Equivalently, an algorithm decides whether each word in the generators represents the identity. -/
def HasSolvableWordProblem (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧
      ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        FreeGroup.mk w ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))

/--
Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?

Here “locally linear” means that every finitely generated subgroup embeds in
$\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$ and some degree $n$, both of which may depend on the
subgroup. Countable includes finite groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G], IsLocallyLinear G →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresented P ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* P, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

namespace variants

/--
Every countable group which is locally linear of bounded degree embeds in a finitely presented
group with solvable word problem.

More precisely, one degree $n$ works for every finitely generated subgroup, while the field may
depend on the subgroup. Solvability of the target's word problem is expressed by the existence of
a finite presentation for which triviality of signed words is a computable predicate.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem bounded_degree :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G],
      (∃ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
        ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (φ : H →* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F),
          Function.Injective φ) →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), HasSolvableWordProblem P ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* P, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

end variants

end Kourovka.«5.16»
modeling_decisions: A finitely presented group is modeled as a group multiplicatively equivalent to `PresentedGroup` for a finite set of relators in the free group on `Fin n`.
A linear group is modeled by an injective group homomorphism into `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F` for an existentially chosen field and degree.
Local linearity quantifies over subgroups satisfying Mathlib's `Subgroup.FG`; both the field and degree may vary with the subgroup.
In the bounded-degree variant, the degree is chosen once outside the subgroup quantifier, while the field remains inside and may vary with the subgroup.

Solvability of the word problem is modeled by computability, on finite signed-generator lists, of membership of `FreeGroup.mk w` in the normal closure of the finite relators. Existence of such a finite presentation is built into the predicate, so the target is also explicitly finitely presented.

Degrees are natural numbers and hence formally permit degree zero. This does not change either property: only the trivial group embeds into degree zero, and it also embeds into degree one over any field.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.16

by F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III

Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?

In (G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III, *Math. Z.* **153** (1977), 117–134) it
is proved that every countable group which is locally linear of bounded degree can be
embedded in a finitely presented group with solvable word problem.

A group is *linear* if it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some
$n \geq 0$ and some field $F$, and *locally linear* if every finitely generated subgroup
is linear (the degree $n$ and the field $F$ may depend on the subgroup). It is *locally
linear of bounded degree* if a single degree $n$ works for all finitely generated subgroups
(the field may still vary).

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 5.16
* [G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III, *Infinitely generated subgroups of
  finitely presented groups. I*, Math. Z. 153 (1977), 117–134](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01179786)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.16»

/-- A group `G` is *linear of degree `n`* if it embeds in the general linear group
$\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$.

The field is taken in `Type`. This loses no generality: the entries of the matrices in the image
of a countable group generate a countable subfield, so a countable linear group of degree `n`
over any field is linear of degree `n` over a field in `Type`. -/
def IsLinearOfDegree (G : Type*) [Group G] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (φ : G →* GL (Fin n) F), Function.Injective φ

/-- A group `G` is *locally linear* if every finitely generated subgroup of `G` is linear
(of some degree, over some field, both possibly depending on the subgroup). -/
def IsLocallyLinear (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → ∃ n : ℕ, IsLinearOfDegree H n

/-- A group `G` is *locally linear of bounded degree* if there is an `n` such that every
finitely generated subgroup of `G` is linear of degree `n` (over some field, possibly depending
on the subgroup). -/
def IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsLinearOfDegree H n

/-- A group `P` is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite
set `rels` of relators in the free group on finitely many generators `Fin n`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- The presentation `⟨Fin n | rels⟩` has *solvable word problem* if the set of words
`w : List (Fin n × Bool)` in the generators and their inverses that represent the identity of
`PresentedGroup rels` is computable (i.e. recursive). -/
def PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) => PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- A group `P` is *finitely presented with solvable word problem* if it has a finite
presentation whose word problem is solvable. (Solvability of the word problem does not depend
on the choice of finite presentation.) -/
def IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* PresentedGroup rels) ∧
    PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem rels

/--
Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?

That is, if $G$ is a countable group all of whose finitely generated subgroups are linear
(each over some field and of some degree), does there exist a finitely presented group $P$
and an injective group homomorphism $G \to P$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G], IsLocallyLinear G →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresented P ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* P, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

/--
Every countable group which is locally linear of bounded degree can be embedded in a
finitely presented group with solvable word problem.

This is the theorem of G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito and C. F. Miller III,
*Math. Z.* **153** (1977), 117–134, cited in the statement of Problem 5.16.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16».variants.bounded_degree :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G], IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree G →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem P ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* P, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

/-- The general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ is linear of degree `n`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLinearOfDegree_generalLinearGroup (n : ℕ) (F : Type) [Field F] :
    IsLinearOfDegree (GL (Fin n) F) n :=
  ⟨F, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id _, fun _ _ h => h⟩

/-- A subgroup of a linear group of degree `n` is linear of degree `n`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLinearOfDegree.subgroup {G : Type*} [Group G] {n : ℕ} (h : IsLinearOfDegree G n)
    (H : Subgroup G) : IsLinearOfDegree H n := by
  obtain ⟨F, _, φ, hφ⟩ := h
  exact ⟨F, inferInstance, φ.comp H.subtype, hφ.comp Subtype.val_injective⟩

/-- A linear group is locally linear of bounded degree. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLinearOfDegree.isLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree {G : Type*} [Group G] {n : ℕ}
    (h : IsLinearOfDegree G n) : IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree G :=
  ⟨n, fun H _ => h.subgroup H⟩

/-- A group which is locally linear of bounded degree is locally linear. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree.isLocallyLinear {G : Type*} [Group G]
    (h : IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree G) : IsLocallyLinear G :=
  fun H hH => h.elim fun n hn => ⟨n, hn H hH⟩

/-- A group given by a finite presentation is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} {rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))}
    (h : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨n, rels, h, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- A finitely presented group with solvable word problem is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem.isFinitelyPresented {P : Type*} [Group P]
    (h : IsFinitelyPresentedWithSolvableWordProblem P) : IsFinitelyPresented P :=
  h.elim fun n ⟨rels, hfin, he, _⟩ => ⟨n, rels, hfin, he⟩

/-- The empty presentation of the trivial group has solvable word problem. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem trivialPresentation_hasSolvableWordProblem :
    PresentationHasSolvableWordProblem (∅ : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0))) :=
  ComputablePred.of_eq (p := fun _ => True) ⟨inferInstance, by simpa using Computable.const true⟩
    fun w => ⟨fun _ => by rw [Subsingleton.elim (FreeGroup.mk w) 1, map_one], fun _ => trivial⟩

end Kourovka.«5.16»
attempts.decomposition_objections: Minor: the note on the primary slot says the statement 'implicitly includes the Higman-necessary condition that G be recursively presented'. For infinitely generated countable groups, recursive presentability is not a necessary condition for embeddability in a finitely presented group (e.g. every subgroup of ℚ, including non-recursively-presentable ones, embeds in a finitely presented group because ℚ does), so no such hypothesis was added; the slot is stated literally as in the notebook. Also, the note for the variant says the solvable-word-problem clause needs a computability notion absent from Mathlib; in fact Mathlib's ComputablePred suffices (and is already used in FormalConjectures/Paper/BranchingVAS.lean), so the clause was included rather than omitted.
modeling_decisions: 'Linear' means embeddable in GL_n(F) for a field F (commutative), with F : Type. Restricting F to universe 0 loses no generality: the matrix entries of the image of a countable group generate a countable subfield, which is equivalent to a type in Type. Similarly G : Type and P : Type are WLOG since G is countable and finitely presented groups are countable.

'Locally linear' is formalized as: every finitely generated subgroup H (H.FG) is linear, with the degree n and the field F allowed to depend on H (any characteristic). 'Locally linear of bounded degree' fixes one n for all f.g. subgroups but lets the field vary. This is the literal reading of the notebook text ('locally linear' + 'of bounded degree'); I could not access the Baumslag–Cannonito–Miller paper (no network) to confirm whether they additionally fix the field. If the paper fixes the field, the variant as stated is stronger than the cited theorem (but still implied by the standard reading of the abstract). Note: 'degree exactly n' vs 'degree ≤ n' are equivalent since GL_m(F) embeds in GL_n(F) for m ≤ n.
'Finitely presented' is ∃ n and a finite set rels ⊆ FreeGroup (Fin n) with P ≃* PresentedGroup rels (Nonempty of the MulEquiv type).

'Solvable word problem' is formalized for a specific finite presentation as ComputablePred (Mathlib's computability notion, w.r.t. the Primcodable encoding of List (Fin n × Bool)) of the set of words representing 1 in PresentedGroup rels. Solvability is independent of the chosen finite presentation, so requiring it for some finite presentation is equivalent to the standard notion.
Countable G includes finite groups, matching group-theoretic usage of 'countable'.

The decomposition notes say recursive presentability of G is 'Higman-necessary'; this is not imposed as a hypothesis (the question is stated for all countable locally linear groups, as in the notebook). Note that for infinitely generated countable groups recursive presentability is not literally necessary (e.g. every subgroup of ℚ embeds in a finitely presented group), so the literal statement is the right one.

/-- A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a quotient of a free group on
finitely many generators by the normal closure of finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- A group is linear if it embeds into $\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$ and
some degree $n$. -/

  ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (n : ℕ)
    (ρ : G →* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F), Function.Injective ρ

/-- A group is locally linear if each of its finitely generated subgroups is linear.

def IsLocallyLinear (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=

/-!
# Conjecture 5.16

by F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III

Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?

In (G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III, *Math. Z.*, **153** (1977), 117–134) it
is proved that every countable group which is locally linear of bounded degree can be
embedded in a finitely presented group with solvable word problem.

Here a group is *linear* if it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $GL_n(F)$ for some $n$ and some
field $F$, and *locally linear* if every finitely generated subgroup is linear (where $n$ and $F$
may depend on the subgroup). It is *locally linear of bounded degree* if a single $n$ works for
all finitely generated subgroups.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 5.16.
- G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III, *Infinitely generated subgroups of finitely
  presented groups. I*, Math. Z. **153** (1977), 117–134.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.16»

universe u

/-- A group $H$ is *linear of degree $n$* if it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $GL_n(F)$ for some
field $F$.

The field $F$ is taken in the same universe as $H$. This loses no generality: if $H$ embeds in
$GL_n(F)$ then it also embeds in $GL_n(F_0)$, where $F_0$ is the subfield of $F$ generated by the
matrix entries of the image of $H$, and $|F_0| \le \max(|H|, \aleph_0)$. -/
def IsLinearGroupOfDegree (H : Type u) [Group H] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (F : Type u) (_ : Field F) (f : H →* GL (Fin n) F), Function.Injective f

/-- A group $H$ is *linear* if it is isomorphic to a subgroup of $GL_n(F)$ for some $n$ and some
field $F$. -/
def IsLinearGroup (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, IsLinearGroupOfDegree H n

/-- A group $G$ is *locally linear* if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is linear. The
degree and the field may depend on the subgroup. -/
def IsLocallyLinear (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsLinearGroup H

/-- A group $G$ is *locally linear of bounded degree* if there is an $n$ such that every finitely
generated subgroup of $G$ is linear of degree $n$. The field may still depend on the subgroup.
Since $GL_m(F)$ embeds in $GL_n(F)$ for $m \le n$, this is the same as asking that the degrees of
the finitely generated subgroups be bounded by $n$. -/
def IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsLinearGroupOfDegree H n

/-- A group $P$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ for some finite set of relators
$r_1, \dots, r_m$ in the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (P ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- A group $P$ has *solvable word problem* if it has a finite generating set $x_1, \dots, x_n$
such that there is an algorithm deciding, for a word $w$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$, whether
$w$ represents the identity of $P$. Decidability is `ComputablePred` from Mathlib. Whether the
word problem is solvable does not depend on the choice of finite generating set. -/
def HasSolvableWordProblem (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : FreeGroup (Fin n) →* P), Function.Surjective f ∧
    ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) => f (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- The general linear group $GL_n(F)$ over a field $F$ is linear of degree $n$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isLinearGroupOfDegree_generalLinearGroup (F : Type u) [Field F] (n : ℕ) :
    IsLinearGroupOfDegree (GL (Fin n) F) n :=
  ⟨F, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id _, Function.injective_id⟩

/-- A group which is locally linear of bounded degree is locally linear. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree.isLocallyLinear {G : Type*} [Group G]
    (h : IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree G) : IsLocallyLinear G :=
  fun H hH => h.elim fun n hn => ⟨n, hn H hH⟩

/-- A group given by a finite presentation is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {n : ℕ} (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/--
Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?

That is, if $G$ is a countable group in which every finitely generated subgroup is isomorphic to
a subgroup of $GL_n(F)$ for some $n$ and some field $F$ (both depending on the subgroup), does
$G$ embed in some finitely presented group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G], IsLocallyLinear G →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresented P ∧
        ∃ f : G →* P, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

/--
Every countable group which is locally linear of bounded degree can be embedded in a finitely
presented group with solvable word problem.

This was proved by G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito and C. F. Miller III,
*Math. Z.* **153** (1977), 117–134.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16».variants.bounded_degree :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G], IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree G →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresented P ∧ HasSolvableWordProblem P ∧
        ∃ f : G →* P, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.16»

  ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (f : G →* GL (Fin n) F), Function.Injective f

/-- A group is *linear* if it is linear of some degree $n$. -/
def IsLinear : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, IsLinearOfDegree G n

the field may depend on the subgroup. -/
def IsLocallyLinear : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsLinear H

generated subgroup is linear of degree $n$. The field may depend on the subgroup. -/

  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsLinearOfDegree H n

for some $n$ and some finite set $R$ of relators in the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. -/

    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

  exact fun H hH => ⟨n, hn H hH⟩

/-!
# Conjecture 5.16

by F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III

Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?

Baumslag, Cannonito, and Miller proved the bounded-degree case, with the stronger
conclusion that the finitely presented group can be chosen to have solvable word problem.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.16»

/-- A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group presented using
finitely many generators and finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresentedGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)

/-- A group is locally linear if every finitely generated subgroup embeds in
$\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$ and some degree $n$, both of which may depend on
the subgroup. -/
def IsLocallyLinear (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
    ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (n : ℕ)
      (f : H →* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F), Function.Injective f

/-- A group is locally linear of bounded degree if there is one degree $n$ such that every
finitely generated subgroup embeds in $\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$ for some field $F$. The field may
vary with the subgroup. -/
def IsLocallyLinearOfBoundedDegree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG →
    ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F)
      (f : H →* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) F), Function.Injective f

/--
Is every countable locally linear group embeddable in a finitely presented group?
Here locally linear means that every finitely generated subgroup has a faithful
finite-dimensional linear representation, with both its field and its degree allowed to vary.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Countable G], IsLocallyLinear G →
      ∃ (P : Type) (_ : Group P), IsFinitelyPresentedGroup P ∧
        ∃ f : G →* P, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

Baumslag, Cannonito, and Miller proved that every countable group which is locally linear
of bounded degree embeds in a finitely presented group with solvable word problem.

The conclusion below records the finitely-presented embedding consequence. The additional
solvable-word-problem conclusion is not represented because Mathlib does not currently provide
